cls: Selective, reversible monoamine oxidase type B (MAO-B) inhibitor
quick: Start 50 mg orally once daily; after 2 weeks may increase to 100 mg once daily
Take once daily at the same time each day, with or without food
Limited data; use only if clearly needed - animal data showed developmental toxicity
Caution; drug/metabolites may pass into milk (animal data) - avoid or weigh risk
No dose adjustment in mild-moderate renal impairment
Max 50 mg/day in moderate impairment; CONTRAINDICATED in severe hepatic impairment
Avoid excessive alcohol; may worsen somnolence
Blood pressure, mood/behavior, dyskinesia, daytime sleepiness, vision in at-risk patients
summary: Safinamide is a selective, reversible MAO-B inhibitor used as add-on therapy to levodopa/carbidopa in Parkinson's disease patients with 'off' episodes. By blocking dopamine breakdown it increases dopaminergic activity. As a MAO-B inhibitor it carries risks of hypertension and serotonin syndrome with many antidepressants and opioids, and is contraindicated with other MAOIs and with severe hepatic impairment.
indications: Adjunctive treatment to levodopa/carbidopa in patients with Parkinson's disease experiencing 'off' episodes

dosage.d: 50 mg once daily at the same time of day
May increase to 100 mg once daily after 2 weeks
dosage.n: Doses above 100 mg give no added benefit and increase adverse effects

dosage.d: Taper 100 mg to 50 mg for 1 week before stopping

admin: Take once daily at approximately the same time each day
May be taken with or without food
Effective only in combination with levodopa/carbidopa
If a dose is missed, take the next dose at the usual time the next day - do not double up
moa: The precise antiparkinsonian mechanism is not fully known. Safinamide selectively and reversibly inhibits monoamine oxidase type B (MAO-B), blocking dopamine catabolism and thereby increasing dopamine levels and dopaminergic activity in the brain. It also has non-dopaminergic effects (modulation of glutamate release via state-dependent sodium-channel blockade).

absolute: Concomitant other MAO inhibitors or potent MAO inhibitors including linezolid (hypertensive crisis)
Concomitant opioids (meperidine and derivatives, methadone, propoxyphene, tramadol)
Concomitant SNRIs; tricyclic, tetracyclic, or triazolopyridine antidepressants; cyclobenzaprine; St. John's wort (serotonin syndrome)
relative: History of psychosis, impulse-control disorders, or major sleepiness
Retinal disease or family history of hereditary retinal disease (animal retinal findings)

preg: There are no adequate human data. Animal studies showed developmental toxicity (including teratogenicity) at clinically relevant exposures. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Safinamide and/or its metabolites were present in milk in animal studies; effects on the breastfed infant are unknown. Decide whether to discontinue nursing or the drug, weighing benefit to the mother.
renal: No dosage adjustment is needed for mild or moderate renal impairment.
hepatic: In moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B) do not exceed 50 mg once daily. Contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C); discontinue if a patient progresses from moderate to severe impairment.

major: Other MAO inhibitors / linezolid (hypertensive crisis) - contraindicated
Serotonergic drugs: SNRIs, TCAs, opioids (tramadol, meperidine, methadone) - serotonin syndrome - contraindicated
moderate: Tyramine-rich foods in very high amounts (>150 mg) can cause hypertension
BCRP substrates (e.g., methotrexate, certain statins) - safinamide inhibits BCRP
minor: Levodopa-induced dyskinesia may be enhanced - may need levodopa dose reduction
interactions.food: No routine tyramine restriction at recommended doses, but avoid foods with very high tyramine content
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excessive alcohol; may potentiate somnolence

serious: Falling asleep during activities of daily living
emergency: Severe allergic reaction with airway swelling

monitoring: Onset of impulse-control disorders or hallucinations
Ophthalmologic monitoring in patients with retinal risk factors
counsel: Take once daily at the same time; do not stop abruptly
Avoid the listed antidepressants, opioids, cough medicines with dextromethorphan, and St. John's wort - tell all prescribers you take this drug
Avoid foods with very high tyramine content (aged cheeses, cured meats, fermented products)
Do not drive if you feel drowsy; report sudden sleep episodes
Report new gambling, shopping, sexual or eating compulsions, or hallucinations
pk: Steady state reached within 5-6 days of daily dosing
pearls: Selectivity for MAO-B is lost at supratherapeutic doses - never exceed 100 mg/day
Has dual dopaminergic (MAO-B) and non-dopaminergic (glutamate/sodium-channel) actions
Routine dietary tyramine restriction is not required at recommended doses, unlike non-selective MAOIs
Taper before stopping to avoid a parkinsonism-hyperpyrexia-like withdrawal syndrome
missed: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the usual time the following day. Do not take two doses to make up for a missed one.
overdose: There is no human overdose experience and no specific antidote. Discontinue safinamide and give supportive care as clinically indicated. Because of MAO-B inhibition, observe dietary tyramine restriction for several weeks after a significant overdose. Contact a poison control center.
